code_summary: This script implements post-training checkpoint-rule selection driven by held-out-user resampling over captured per-epoch validation predictions. Existing menu primitives can force checkpoint averaging (for example n_checkpoints plus checkpoint_combine), but they cannot evaluate alternative epoch-selection rules from one trajectory using held-out users, nor can they choose among those rules without reusing the same validation users for both selection and scoring. code_summary: Implements held-out-user checkpoint-selection-rule testing on one training run by capturing per-epoch validation predictions, defining callable rules (best epoch and top-N averaging), passing them to selection_rule_test, then materialising the chosen rule's averaged validation scores. rationale.idea: Increase only the FM embedding dimension from the incumbent recipe to test whether capacity is still a live lever inside the BPR+history+temporal branch.
rationale.why_expected_to_help: BPR plus recency-weighted history and hour+dow introduces more interaction structure than the plain baseline recipe, so a wider FM may capture additional useful cross-field interactions even though earlier broad k sweeps were near-null; conversely, if this also fails, it usefully confirms that capacity is not the bottleneck in the strongest branch either.
rationale.grounded_in: Specific prior evidence is mixed enough to justify a scoped confirmation: the menu's training axis includes k32 with the note 'tested ~neutral; only useful combined with new signal sources', while the measured dead-end says 'Raising FM embedding dim k=8/16/32: 0.5895/0.5902/0.5887 — no gain' but also explicitly warns that this was about embedding capacity only. In this project's own history, a closely related k=32 run inside the strong branch scored 0.6040 versus ~0.6053 then-best, but it also changed checkpoint settings ('k':32, 'patience':4, 'n_checkpoints':5, 'checkpoint_combine':true), so the capacity question is not perfectly isolated for the exact incumbent recipe.
